narrative.overview: The interface is a cabinet of dark, slightly olive steel slabs trimmed with thin bronze, laid over a full-screen map. It follows Hearts of Iron IV's topology exactly, because the players already know it: top bar, left slide-out panels, outliner on the right, map modes at the bottom right. All art is original. Density is high: numbers are read at a glance, and every element explains itself through a rich tooltip.
keyCharacteristics: Bronze hairline borders, with brighter bronze for active state.
Condensed caps for headers and labels, condensed tabular numerals for values.
Cream ink on steel; green, red and amber only where they carry meaning.
Rich tooltips (title band plus rows) on every readout, tile and table row.

rules.name: The Meaningful Colour Rule
rules.body: Green (good), red (bad) and amber (warn) appear only on values that are actually improving, worsening or in a warning state, such as stat flashes and interest group approval. Never use them as decoration.

rules.name: The Data Colour Rule
rules.body: Party, ideology and country colours come from the game data. The shell never recolours them; it frames them in black hairlines so they read on steel.

rules.name: The Heading-First Rule
rules.body: A name or heading leads, and its role or date follows beneath it. No small label sits above a heading.

rules.name: The Bevel-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Containers are bevelled steel slabs with hairline edges, never rounded cards with soft shadows, and never nested cards.

dos: Do put every new system in its HOI4 position: its tab in the top row, its panel on the left, lists in the outliner, map overlays in the map-mode cluster.
Do give every number a tooltip that explains where it comes from.
Do show unbuilt systems honestly, with the phase that adds them.
Do use the authored icon set (24px grid, 1.6 stroke) for any new icon.
donts: Don't round corners or use glass, gradients on text, or soft floating cards.
Don't place small labels or eyebrows above headings, or coloured side stripes on list items.
Don't use Paradox-owned art, icons, fonts or textures.
Don't decorate with loaded political or military symbols.
